A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CRISP for single-positive multi-label learning. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite revisions and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments on ten datasets, significance tests, sensitivity analyses, ablations, and attention-map case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional baseline comparisons, validation-prior ablations, timing measurements, and prior-update-frequency experiments.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a class-dependent logit adjustment in Eq. (8), replacing the positive-loss term 1-f^j(x) with 1-sigmoid(g^j(x)-lambda(1-pi^j)). This substantively changes the optimized objective. AN warm-up already appeared in v1 Appendix A.5; its addition to Algorithm 1 is documentation, not a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four image datasets—VOC, COCO, NUS, and CUB—and six MLL datasets—Image, Scene, Yeast, Corel5k, Mirflickr, and Delicious. The added analyses retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds MIME and LL-R/LL-CP/LL-CT to both benchmark groups, and three BoostLU+LL combinations to the image comparisons. MIME and LL also enter the Yeast prior-prediction comparison. LAGC is renamed PLC: the cited work and all four Table 1 scores match, so this is not a replacement baseline.

E3.justification: The principal splits and predictive metrics remain unchanged. New controls estimate priors from fully labeled validation data or update them every three epochs; the fixed-prior sweep changes from 0.1–0.9 to 0.001–0.3. Some sensitivity settings are unresolved: v2 Figure 2a displays delta values from 0.1 to 10, while Section 5.3.2 states 0.001–0.1.

E4.justification: v2 adds validation-derived-prior comparisons across both benchmark groups, prior-update-frequency and computational-cost analyses, and sensitivity analysis for lambda. It revises the fixed-prior ablation and expands the Yeast prior-prediction comparison. Conversely, v1's attention-map case studies are removed; the existing image-dataset convergence analysis is retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A.6 newly states that the comparing methods run five trials on each dataset. Both versions already report means and standard deviations and use Wilcoxon signed-ranks tests at 0.05. The disclosure does not establish an increase in runs, and additional test columns retain the existing statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces CRISP's VOC/COCO/NUS/CUB mAP values of 89.820/74.640/49.996/21.650 with 89.931/74.913/50.045/22.150 alongside the revised objective; these are not established same-method gains. CUB changes from second place to first. Original MLL result rows remain unchanged, while substantial baseline, ablation, and timing results are added. v2 Table 12 contains 53 wins among 60 tests, although Section 5.2 incorrectly states 43.

T1.justification: The two principal theorems and most appendix derivations are retained. Theorem 4.1 restricts delta to (0,1), replacing v1's delta >= 0, and Appendix A.5 removes an extra class summation from one complexity-bound proof step. Theorem 4.2 still analyzes the unadjusted objective, not the newly introduced lambda-adjusted loss.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: class-prior estimation, an unbiased risk estimator with approximate consistency guarantees, and superior SPMLL performance on ten datasets. The additional method component and experiments do not substantially redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies prior convergence with a classifier-dependent residual error and qualifies risk convergence using the complexity terms, where v1's accompanying explanations asserted convergence directly. It adds mechanisms involving rare-class bias and AN warm-up, explanations concerning validation-set estimation instability, and computational-efficiency arguments. The attention-based interpretation about detecting small objects is removed.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's warm-up, PyTorch, and RTX 3090 disclosures, v2 Appendix A.6 specifies Adam, batch-size choices, ten epochs, learning-rate and weight-decay search ranges, fixed delta/tau values, validation-based selection, and ResNet-50 backbones. Appendix A.2 explains threshold search over classifier outputs, and Table 4 adds timing information. These are substantial documentation additions, not evidence that all retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit connections to Garg et al.'s PU mixture-proportion estimation and Zhao et al.'s distribution-based PU learning, plus references supporting MIME, LL, and BoostLU comparisons. The main related-work survey and overall SPMLL positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 merges the preliminary subsections, revises selected method and interpretation passages, reorganizes supplementary subsections, and adds an impact statement. It also changes author order, baseline terminology, and citation style. Much of the introduction, related work, contribution list, and conclusion retains its wording and structure.

P2.justification: v2 expands comparison tables and Figure 1, adds timing and ablation tables, and relocates Coverage and Wilcoxon displays to the appendix. It removes the attention-map figure and redistributes sensitivity panels, while retaining v1's convergence Figure 4 as Figure 3. Some revised labeling is inconsistent: Figure 2b depicts the fixed-prior ablation but is titled lambda sensitivity.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons, validation-prior and update-frequency controls, and substantially better implementation documentation make v2 more informative and assessable than v1. These benefits are tempered by the absence of a guarantee for the new adjusted objective and new reporting inconsistencies, including the sensitivity-plot labels/ranges and the win count contradicting Table 12. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
